# Device Claims Review: Public Web Copy for Home Blood-Pressure Monitor

**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09
**Device / IVD:** Home Blood-Pressure Monitor — Class IIa (assumed)
**Intended purpose (as assessed):** NOT SUPPLIED — limb (d) not assessed
**Audience:** Publikum (un-gated consumer web page)
**Markets:** Germany

---

## Summary

3 claims reviewed. 1 cut, 1 verify, 1 OK.

**Ready to publish:** With changes below

---

## Findings

### 1. "Don't gamble with your heart"
**Claim:** "Don't gamble with your heart"
**Breach:** HWG § 11(1) no. 7 [verified], MDR Art. 7(b) [verified]
**Why:** It suggests that health is compromised by *not* using the device (breaching the prohibition on fear-of-not-using framing under HWG § 11(1) no. 7) and implies a preventative clinical benefit/outcome that a monitoring-only device cannot deliver on its own (breaching MDR Art. 7(b)).
**Evidence needed:** n/a — cannot be cured by evidence
**Also engaged:** none
**Call:** Cut
**Suggested fix:** Remove the alarmist framing entirely. Focus on proactive, objective tracking:
> "Track your blood pressure daily to support your heart health"

---

### 2. "Recommended by Professor Schmidt, cardiologist."
**Claim:** "Recommended by Professor Schmidt, cardiologist."
**Breach:** none
**Why:** Professional recommendations are not prohibited for medical devices under German law (for devices, HWG § 11(1) is restricted to nos. 7–9, 11, and 12; the restriction on professional endorsements in no. 2 does not apply to devices).
**Evidence needed:** Documented proof of Professor Schmidt’s actual credentials, the written endorsement, and active consent to use his name/title in this marketing material.
**
